info.title: TeamPass REST API
info.description: Collaborative password manager REST API. Authenticate via POST /authorize (login + password + apikey) or POST /authorizeToken (OAuth2 Personal Access Token), then pass the returned JWT as 'Authorization: Bearer <jwt>'. Errors use the RFC 9457 application/problem+json envelope; the legacy 'error' member is kept for backward compatibility.

servers.description: Legacy unversioned base path (treated as v1)

post.summary: Get a JWT from login + password + API key
Get a JWT from a Personal Access Token (OAuth2/SSO users)

post.description: Flags the api_sessions row matching the token's jti as revoked — the JWT is then rejected on every endpoint until it expires. Legacy tokens without a session row invalidate the user's single legacy API session instead.

get.summary: Get item(s) by id, label or description
get.description: Exactly one of 'id', 'label' or 'description' is required. 'label' and 'description' lookups are searches: they accept 'like', 'limit' and 'offset' and return X-Total-Count.

get.summary: Get items contained in a list of folders

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Comma-separated or JSON array of folder ids

200.description: Items in the requested folders (empty array when none)

get.summary: Get the current TOTP code of an item
Changes to apply to a client cache since a revision
get.description: Delta feed for offline clients. Returns the items that changed after the given revision, and the ones the client must drop. Cursor based: store the returned cursor and pass it as `since` on the next call, repeating while `has_more` is true. A `full_sync_required` of true means the cursor cannot be served — read the vault through item/inFolders and adopt the returned cursor. Start there on a first synchronization, with `since=0`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Cursor returned by the previous call, exclusive. 0 on a first synchronization.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum journal entries scanned in one call.

cursor.description: Cursor to store and send as `since` on the next call.

has_more.description: More changes are waiting: call again with the returned cursor.

full_sync_required.description: The cursor cannot be served. Rebuild the cache and adopt the returned cursor.

revision_changed_at.description: Unix UTC timestamp in seconds of the winning journal revision.

reason.description: deleted: soft deleted. purged: permanently removed. out_of_scope: still exists but no longer readable by the caller.

post.description: All listed fields must be present, even if empty. Idempotency-Key is optional; within the configured offline synchronization window (90 days by default, 0 for no limit) the same user, key and canonical creation intent return the original 201 response without repeating side effects.

Location.description: Path-absolute reference of the created resource (item/get?id=N)

put.description: Requires 'id' plus at least one updatable field (label, password, description, login, email, url, tags, anyone_can_modify, icon, folder_id, totp, fields). Moving an item out of a personal folder into a shared one redistributes its encryption keys synchronously, so it must be requested on its own: combining it with any other updatable field returns 422. It returns 422 as well when a source encryption key cannot be recovered (the item stays personal), and 409 when the item was modified concurrently.

revision.description: Revision of the item after the update

revision_changed_at.description: Unix UTC timestamp in seconds paired with the returned revision; null when the date is unknown.

delete.description: The optional revision is an optimistic-concurrency precondition. Idempotency-Key makes a successful deletion replayable for the configured offline synchronization window (90 days by default, 0 for no limit) without allocating another revision or repeating side effects.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Current item revision expected by the caller. A mismatch returns 409 before any mutation; an empty value is treated as omitted.

revision_changed_at.description: Unix UTC timestamp paired with the deletion revision

get.summary: List the folder tree accessible to the user
get.description: Returns a hierarchical tree. Pagination ('offset'/'limit') applies to the root-level entries; X-Total-Count is the total number of root entries.

200.description: Folder tree (empty array when the user has no accessible folder)

get.summary: List accessible folders with item and folder-management capabilities
get.description: Historical name — returns ALL accessible folders. access_type, is_readonly, can_create, can_edit and can_delete describe operations on items contained in the folder. The can_*_folder fields describe folder-management UI capabilities and never replace the authoritative checks performed by POST /folder/create, PUT /folder/update and DELETE /folder/delete. Rows are ordered by 'position' (MPTT pre-order), so parent_id + level + position rebuild the exact folder hierarchy, sibling order included.

201.description: Folder created (no Location header: the API has no folder get-by-id endpoint yet; the body carries newId)

put.description: PUT only. Every field except 'id' is optional; unspecified fields keep their current value. 'access_rights' is not updatable here (roles-management concern). Personal root folders cannot be renamed or moved, and cross-domain (personal ↔ shared) moves are rejected.

delete.summary: Soft-delete a folder and its descendants
delete.description: DELETE only. The folder and all its descendants go to the recycle bin (restorable from Utilities → Recycled bin); contained items are soft-deleted. Personal root folders and folder id 0 cannot be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Folder id to delete (may also be sent in the JSON body)

200.description: User list (sensitive columns are never returned)

post.summary: Get browser extension connection settings (POST variant)

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Opaque 1-128 character visible-ASCII key, scoped to the authenticated user and API operation. Raw keys are never persisted.

X-Total-Count.description: Total number of matching entries before pagination

Idempotency-Replayed.description: Present with value true when the stored response was replayed without executing the mutation.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details; the legacy 'error' member duplicates 'detail' for backward compatibility.

revision.description: Monotonic revision of the item, bumped on every content change. Compare it against a cached copy to detect staleness; the larger value is the newer one.

revision_changed_at.description: Unix UTC timestamp in seconds paired with revision. It changes on functional content revisions, never on reads or ciphertext-only rewrites; null means the date is unknown.

revision.description: Monotonic revision of the item, bumped on every content change. Compare it against a cached copy to detect staleness; the larger value is the newer one.

revision_changed_at.description: Unix UTC timestamp in seconds paired with revision; null when the date is unknown.

CustomField.description: A custom field value attached to an item. Fields restricted via 'Restrict Visibility to' (categories.role_visibility) are omitted entirely for users holding none of the required roles; their value is never decrypted nor returned. No admin bypass.

totp.description: Base32 secret or otpauth://totp provisioning URI

revision.description: Optional precondition, not an updatable field: the revision the edit was based on. The update is refused with 409 when the server has moved on since. Omitting it keeps the previous last-writer-wins behaviour.

totp.description: Base32 secret, otpauth://totp provisioning URI, or an empty string to remove TOTP

parent_id.description: Parent folder id (0 = root, requires user_can_create_root_folder). Optional when 'private' is true — defaults to the caller's personal root.

complexity.description: Password complexity level. Required for a shared target; optional (default 0) when the resolved target is personal (e.g. 'private' is true).

private.description: Optional. When true, creates a personal (private) folder under the caller's personal root without needing its id (requires personal folders to be enabled for the user). The personal_folder flag is never accepted directly from the client — it is derived server-side from the resolved parent.

access_rights.description: Access level granted to the caller's roles on the new folder. Defaults to W when omitted.

parent_id.description: New parent id (move). Cross-domain personal ↔ shared moves are rejected (422).

complexity.description: Password complexity level. Must be one of the TeamPass levels; any other value is rejected with 422.

revision.description: Revision allocated to the new item

revision_changed_at.description: Unix UTC timestamp in seconds paired with the allocated revision; null when the date is unknown.

deleted_folders.description: Ids of the folder and every descendant that was soft-deleted.

complexity.description: Minimum password strength required for items in this folder. 0 when no rule is set.

position.description: MPTT left bound. The list is already sorted on it; use it to restore tree order after a client-side re-sort.

complexity.description: Minimum password strength required for items in this folder. 0 when no rule is set.

is_readonly.description: 1 when the resolved item access type is R. ND/NE/NDNE are NOT read-only — check can_edit and can_delete.

access_type.description: Effective access level for items contained in this folder, least-permissive-wins across all the user's roles (R > NDNE > NE = ND > W).

can_create.description: Item right: 1 when the user may create an item in this folder (false only for R). This does not authorize creating a subfolder.

can_edit.description: Item right: 1 when the user may edit existing items in this folder (false for NE, NDNE and R). This does not authorize renaming or moving the folder.

can_delete.description: Item right: 1 when the user may delete items in this folder (false for ND, NDNE and R). This does not authorize deleting the folder.

is_personal.description: 1 when the folder is part of a personal folder tree; 0 for the shared domain. This endpoint only ever lists the caller's own personal folders, so in practice 1 means 'mine'.

is_personal_root.description: 1 for the protected root of the personal folder domain. A personal root cannot be renamed, moved or deleted.

can_create_subfolder.description: Folder-management hint: 1 when POST /folder/create may use this folder as its parent according to the current access, read-only state, API create permission and global folder-management rules. The create route performs the final validation.

can_rename_folder.description: Folder-management hint: 1 when the source folder is eligible for rename according to the current access, read-only state, API update permission, global folder-management rules and personal-root protection. PUT /folder/update performs the final validation.

can_move_folder.description: Folder-management hint for the source only: 1 when the source folder is eligible to move. PUT /folder/update separately validates the chosen destination, including access, read-only state, cycles, personal/shared domain boundaries and root permission.

can_delete_folder.description: Folder-management hint: 1 when the source folder is eligible for deletion according to the current access, read-only state, API delete permission, global folder-management rules and personal-root protection. DELETE /folder/delete performs the final validation.

teampass_version.description: Complete TeamPass server release version returned in the response body, outside the JWT.

teampass_version_major.description: Base TeamPass server version (major.minor.patch) returned in the response body.

teampass_version_minor.description: Final TeamPass release revision component returned in the response body.

teampass_version.description: Complete TeamPass server release version, refreshed independently of authentication.

MethodNotAllowed.description: HTTP method not supported for this endpoint (Allow header lists supported methods)

Conflict.description: The resource changed while the request was being processed

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (api_rate_limit_per_minute, per user and per IP)

HttpsRequired.description: Request rejected because api_require_https is enabled and the request was sent over plain HTTP
